T: Crème de la crème. Hold the sleeping pills.
D: A family of pampered Paris cats is dumped in the countryside by the butler and finds its way home with an alley cat.
P: Serve dessert when Edgar the butler prepares the cream.
S: Wedges of blue cheese on a board with sliced pears, toasted walnuts, a pot of honey and crackers.

Choux pastry with gruyère piped into small balls, baked at 200C for 20 minutes until puffed. Bring 125ml water, 125ml milk, 100g butter and a pinch of salt to the boil. Tip in 150g plain flour and beat over the heat for 2 minutes until the dough comes away from the sides. Cool 5 minutes, then beat in 4 eggs one at a time until glossy. Stir in 120g grated gruyère, a pinch of nutmeg and pepper. Pipe walnut-size balls onto lined trays, top with a little more cheese and bake at 200C for 20 minutes until puffed and golden.
the alley cats jamming in the Paris attic
Mini croque monsieurs of ham, gruyère, Dijon and béchamel on white bread, grilled until bubbling and cut into squares.
M: the cats lost in the French countryside
Chicken thighs browned and simmered with bacon, mushrooms and red wine for 90 minutes, with buttery mash.
Abigail and Amelia's chicken leek pie
Abigail and Amelia, the English geese

Chicken, leek and mushroom pie in a creamy sauce under puff pastry, baked at 200C for 25 minutes. Brown 800g diced chicken thigh in 30g butter and set aside. Cook 1 sliced leek and 200g sliced mushrooms for 6 minutes. Stir in 2 tbsp plain flour, then 300ml chicken stock and 150ml cream and simmer until thick. Add the chicken and thyme and season. Spoon into a pie dish, cover with 1 sheet puff pastry, brush with egg and bake at 200C for 25 minutes until golden. Serve with buttered peas.
W: the bowl of cream Edgar serves the cats
Vanilla crème brûlée baked at 150C for 35 minutes in a water bath, chilled, sugar torched on top. Nothing added.
K: the cats riding in the back of the milk truck

Cold milk blended with vanilla ice cream, honey and a vanilla bean until frothy, poured into glasses with a pinch of nutmeg on top. Split 1 vanilla bean and scrape the seeds into a blender, or use 1 tsp vanilla bean paste. Add 600ml cold full cream milk, 4 scoops vanilla ice cream and 2 tbsp honey and blend for 30 seconds until frothy. Pour into 4 glasses and dust with a little grated nutmeg. Serve straight away.

s.how: Set a wedge of blue cheese at room temperature on a wooden board. Slice 2 pears thinly and fan them beside it. Add toasted walnuts, a pot of honey and water crackers. A board fit for a mouse with very good taste.

s.note: the alley cats jamming in the Paris attic
s.how: Make a quick bechamel with 30g butter, a spoon of flour and 250ml milk. Spread bread with Dijon, fill with ham and grated gruyere, then top with bechamel and more cheese. Grill until bubbling and cut into small squares. Serve on a silver tray.

m.note: the cats lost in the French countryside
m.how: Brown 1kg chicken thighs and 150g diced bacon. Add 250g mushrooms and cook until golden, then pour in 500ml red wine and water to cover. Simmer for 90 minutes until rich and glossy. Serve over mash from 1kg potatoes and butter.

w.note: the bowl of cream Edgar serves the cats
w.how: Heat 600ml cream with a split vanilla bean until steaming. Whisk 6 yolks with 80g sugar, pour in the cream and strain into ramekins. Bake in a water bath at 150C for 35 minutes and chill. Sprinkle with sugar and torch until amber. Nothing added.

d.note: the cats riding in the back of the milk truck
d.how: Split 1 vanilla bean and scrape the seeds into a blender, or use 1 tsp vanilla bean paste. Add 600ml cold full cream milk, 4 scoops vanilla ice cream and 2 tbsp honey and blend for 30 seconds until frothy. Pour into 4 glasses and dust with a little grated nutmeg. Serve straight away.
